rationale: INCOMING_PY (ontology workstream). PY-14 added the TUPLE spelling of `__all__` and left the third one: the grammar gives a bare comma-separated RHS its own node, `expression_list`, so `__all__ = "a", "b"` was neither the `list` nor the `tuple` the allowlist read and published NOTHING. The language HAS the declaration — `from mod import *` honours it identically — so by the workstream's own table this is a GAP and not a RULED verdict. Falsifiable measurement: `script/m60/python-construct-probe.ts` counts 238 `__all__` assignments in CPython 3.10's stdlib and 9 of them use this spelling (3.8%); on the pinned bb_tests corpus the count is 0, reported as 0. `dunderAllForm` is pinned because that is the field that lets this revert be expressed as a SHAPE (`expression_list` out of the allowlist) rather than as a list of fixture strings. The two forbid rows are the boundaries that remain: a concatenation and a comprehension both need an expression evaluated, and this lane does no data flow — pinning the absence means closing either one later has to update this file deliberately.

expectRelationships.note: THE GAP. `expression_list` is the spelling the allowlist did not read
a LEADING UNDERSCORE IS NOT A FILTER — the author put it in `__all__`, so it is exported. Same rule the list/tuple fixture pins

forbidRelationships.note: DECLARED BOUNDARY: the concatenation `__all__ = "coroutine" + (...)` is a binary expression, not a literal. Evaluating it is a data-flow question
DECLARED BOUNDARY: a list comprehension has no statically knowable member list, and `name` is its loop variable rather than a declared export either

_seamNote.what: exports are derived SYNTACTICALLY from a `list`, `tuple` or `expression_list` literal assigned directly to `__all__` at module scope. All three spellings reach `from mod import *` identically, which is why they are one relation and not three.
_seamNote.why: Adding the third spelling adds no new KIND of claim: the set of names is read off a literal either way, and the shape that decides it is answerable from the grammar rather than by evaluating anything. `dunderAllForm` records which spelling declared a name because a module may declare its surface twice in two forms, and a reader triaging the surface wants to see that.
_seamNote.evidenceClass: structural — the link between a module and a name it declares is read from the module's own AST, not inferred across a boundary.
